3080.name: NOM1
3080.text: You folks are very brave, but no one can survive out here without money to buy food and supplies. I collected $100.00 from your neighbors to help you through the winter. I'm sure you would do the same for us.

3081.name: NoM2
3081.text: Take money out of the box under your bed.

3082.name: NoM3
3082.text: After all your hard work, it's a shame not to sell your crops. It's no wonder that you ran out of money. I think you should sell your crops right away.

3083.name: NoM4
3083.text: Hello, neighbor. You look as though you could use some advice. You can use your homestead claim as security to borrow money from the bank.

3084.name: NOM5
3084.text: I'm sorry to hear that you're heading back east. We heard that you ran out of money. I collected $50.00 from your neighbors to help pay for your journey. I hope you'll come back next year and try again.

3085.name: NOM6
3085.text: I'm sorry to hear that you're heading back east. We heard that you ran out of money. I hope you'll come back next year and try again.

3110.text:
March, 1880
We're ready to say good-bye to city life on the
East Coast.  We'll travel first by train and then 
by covered wagon to the High Plains of Kansas.
Once we're there, we'll  stake a claim for a 
homestead of 160 acres. Our family is ready to
go west and make a new start!

3112.name: MyText
3112.text:
March, 1880
We're ready to say good-bye to city life on the East Coast.  We'll travel first by train and then by covered wagon to the High Plains of Kansas. Once we're there, we'll stake a claim for a homestead of 160 acres. Our family is ready to go west and make a new start!

3113.text:
April, 1880
We've finally made it to Kansas!  We've found a  good spot for our homestead, not far from a creek  and a small town.  Until we build a house, we're  living in a tent made from the top of our covered wagon.  Once we get settled, we'll get ready to farm our homestead.

3257.name: NewHouse
3257.text: Hi, neighbor. Did you know that you can afford some new furniture for your house? It will help make even the plainest sod house prettier. New furniture costs $200.00. Would you like to buy it?

3283.text:
2. Class: Edunetics
This is the root of the Edunetics class library. It is an abstract class that gives it’s offspring the following capabilities: 
· Self documentation (describe)
· Self destruction (dispose)
· Self name (getName)
2.1. Cardinality: 0

2.2.  Attributes:

2.2.1.  Symbol psyName 
Object identity.
2.3. Methods:

2.3.1. birth
Lingo constructor
2.3.1.1. Return Value: Object
The new object
2.3.1.2. Parameters:
2.3.1.2.1. me
Self pointer Lingo style
2.3.1.2.2. Symbol syName
The identity of the new object
2.3.2. vDescribe
Print the description text on the message window (Director)
2.3.2.1. Return Value: Void
<Description>
2.3.2.2. Parameters:
2.3.2.2.1. me
Lingo syntax.
2.3.3. plObjectToList
Return the current state of the instance propeties as a property list where each property of the object is a property in the list and the same goes for values. If one of the values is an object by itself, it will be also replaced with such a property lis
2.3.3.1. Return Value: PropertyList
A property list with the current instance propeties' values.
2.3.3.2. Parameters:
2.3.3.2.1. LingoObject oMe
Lingo syntax.
2.3.4. syListToProperties
Update an instance properties value from a propety list.
2.3.4.1. Return Value: Symbol
#OK or #ERR_ListToProperties_PropertyNotExist:XX or #ERR_ListToProperties_WrongValue:XX
2.3.4.2. Parameters:
2.3.4.2.1. LingoObject oMe
The object to update.
2.3.4.2.2. PropertyList plNewValues
Each property must have a property in the object. The values will be stored in the matching property of the object.
2.3.5. vDispose
Do the clean-up of the object. User should assign it to the object for disposing.
2.3.5.1. Return Value: Void
<Description>
2.3.5.2. Parameters:
2.3.5.2.1. me
Lingo syntax.
End of Class 'Edunetics'
